name: K Health
one_liner: App-based doctors who can prescribe non-controlled medication for anxiety and depression after an AI symptom check; $49 first month.
best_for: Adults with mild to moderate anxiety or depression who want to start or continue an antidepressant
People without insurance who want a flat monthly price for medication visits
People who want primary care and mental health medication in one app
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People with severe depression, bipolar disorder or other high-risk conditions, which K Health refers to in-person care
Anyone seeking Xanax or other controlled medications
People who want ongoing talk therapy (K Health refers out for therapy)
short_description: Telehealth membership where clinicians treat anxiety and depression with non-controlled medication, after an AI intake; $49 first month, then $147.
long_description: K Health is a telehealth service run through an app. You start with an AI chat that asks about your symptoms, then see a K Health clinician by text or video. In its mental health program a clinician may prescribe medication for anxiety or depression, suggest self-guided resources, or refer you to a therapist or psychiatrist; K Health does not offer ongoing therapy itself, does not prescribe controlled substances such as Xanax, and does not treat bipolar disorder or severe depression remotely. The membership is $49 for the first month and then renews at $147 every three months; a one-time visit is $73, medication is extra and shipping is $12 a month. It generally does not take insurance, except some Surest and Elevance Health plans. It serves adults in 48 states. K Health's privacy policy says it may 'sell' and 'share' some personal information, including with advertising partners; you can opt out through 'Your Privacy Choices'. A 2025 study in Annals of Internal Medicine looked at its AI in virtual urgent care, not mental health.
patient_summary: You chat with K Health's AI about your symptoms, then message or video-chat with a clinician who can prescribe non-controlled medication for anxiety or depression. It costs $49 for the first month and then $147 every three months, or $73 for a one-time visit; medication is extra and most insurance isn't accepted. It is for adults, and you'll be referred elsewhere for therapy or for severe or complex conditions.

pricing.starting_price: $49/month (billed $147 every 3 months after a $49 first month); $73 one-time visit
pricing.notes: Medication is not included; shipping from K Health is $12/month, or use your own pharmacy and insurance for the medication. K Health generally does not accept insurance for memberships or visits, except certain Surest and Elevance Health plans.

privacy.notes: Medical records fall under a joint HIPAA notice, but the privacy policy says K Health may 'sell' and 'share' identifiers and browsing data with ad partners; deletion rights are offered only to residents of states with privacy laws.

seo.title: K Health: AI Telehealth Review & Pricing | HeyPsych
seo.meta_description: K Health offers AI-assisted primary care and mental health treatment with real doctors, providing anxiety and depression medication for affordable prices.

faqs.q: How does K Health use AI?
faqs.a: K Health's AI analyzes your symptoms based on data from millions of patient records to help identify potential conditions. You then connect with a real doctor who makes treatment decisions. The AI assists but doesn't replace physician care.

faqs.q: How much does K Health mental health cost?
faqs.a: K Health offers $49/year membership for unlimited free assessments. Mental health visits cost approximately $49-73 per visit on top of membership. Medications are additional. Some insurance plans are also accepted.

faqs.q: What mental health medications can K Health prescribe?
faqs.a: K Health prescribes common anxiety and depression medications including SSRIs and non-controlled anti-anxiety medications. They don't prescribe controlled substances. A licensed physician evaluates your needs during the consultation.

Yes, K Health uses licensed physicians and has millions of users. The AI is a tool that helps providers work efficiently. For straightforward anxiety and depression, it's a legitimate affordable option. Complex conditions may need more specialized care.

clinical_trials.study: Retrospective study of K Health's AI recommendations in AI-assisted virtual urgent care at Cedars-Sinai Connect (not a mental health study)

citation.authors: Zeltzer D, Kugler Z, Hayat L, Brufman T, Ilan Ber R, Leibovich K, Beer T, Frank I, Shaul R, Goldzweig C, Pevnick J
citation.title: Comparison of Initial Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Final Physician Recommendations in AI-Assisted Virtual Urgent Care Visits

clinical_trials.outcome: AI and final physician recommendations matched in 56.8% of visits; covers respiratory, urinary, eye and dental complaints, not anxiety or depression.

primary_uses: Starting or refilling antidepressant or anti-anxiety medication (non-controlled)
Anxiety and depression check-ins with a clinician by text or video
AI symptom check before a visit
Referral to a therapist or psychiatrist

availability.note: Adults 18+ in 48 states. No controlled substances; severe or high-risk conditions are referred to in-person care.
